items.title: Ironically, the Blue Wave Could Make Hyperscalers “Good Businesses Again” by Forcing Capex Discipline
items.summary: Key TakeawaysDemocrats won control of the House and Senate in Tuesday’s midterms, and state results point to more limits on building data centers but fewer outright bans. Tighter rules that slow the build-out would help Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft shareholders, because less capex while capacity stays scarce repairs free cash flow without hurting demand.

items.title: Top VC: The Best AI Models Take “80% Plus” of Spend. And Alphabet’s Gemini Just Ranked No. 1
items.summary: Key TakeawaysAlphabet’s Gemini 4 Carbon now ranks first on Artificial Analysis’s Intelligence Index, and a16z’s Martin Casado says the best frontier models take more than 80% of AI spending, weighted by dollars. The ranking hasn’t won Alphabet that spending yet: Anthropic and OpenAI hold 86% of enterprise API spend, and few customers can use Carbon so far.

items.summary: Key TakeawaysAMD beat third-quarter estimates as data center revenue climbed 97% to $8. 5 billion, and it guided to about $17 billion of fourth-quarter revenue.
